worked_example.problem: Why could Neolithic people stay in one place, when earlier people kept moving?
steps: Earlier people followed wild animals and plants, so they had to move.
Neolithic people grew crops and kept animals, so food was near them all year.
So they could build permanent villages.
worked_example.answer: Because farming and herding gave them food in one place.

cards.idea: In the New Stone Age, people began to farm crops and keep animals.
example: Goats, sheep and cattle were domesticated; millet and sorghum were grown.

cards.idea: Farming let people live in permanent villages, with polished stone tools and pottery.
example: Clay pots stored grain and water.

cards.idea: More food meant more people, trade and people with special skills such as potters and weavers.
example: A village with extra grain could trade it for salt or tools.
